verdict: Salesforce closed its fiscal year with revenue up 11% to $9.29B and net income of $1.45B — versus a loss a year ago — then used the moment to launch its first-ever dividend and add $10B to its buyback.

segments.note: The core software subscriptions — Sales, Service, Slack, Tableau and Data Cloud.

otherDetail: A $35M loss on strategic investments (stakes Salesforce holds in other companies), partly offset by $58M of other income — mostly interest earned, net of interest on Salesforce's debt: a net $23M.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: A steady finish to the fiscal year
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 11% from a year ago to $9.29B, led by subscription and support at $8.75B, up 12%. Professional services shrank 9% to $539M. Current remaining performance obligations — work signed but not yet billed — rose 12% to $27.6B.

takeaways.title: From a loss to $1.47 a share
takeaways.text: Net income was $1.45B, versus a $98M loss a year ago when restructuring charges peaked; GAAP EPS swung from -$0.10 to $1.47. Fourth-quarter operating cash flow was $3.40B, up 22%, and free cash flow $3.26B.

takeaways.title: Salesforce's first-ever dividend
takeaways.text: Salesforce declared its first quarterly dividend of $0.40 a share and added $10B to its share-buyback authorization — a marker of its shift toward returning cash to shareholders as growth settles to around 10%.
